Act I · Why this existsClinical referenceExternal evidence

Screening demand outgrows specialist time

ICO 2017 · §1

1 in 3

people with diabetes have some form of diabetic retinopathy.

ICO 2017 · §1

Visual loss may be absent in early retinopathy, so regular screening is essential for early intervention.

ICO 2017 · §2.1

Using ophthalmologists to screen every person with diabetes is an inefficient use of resources.

ICO 2017 · §3.1.3

Fundus photography creates a permanent record, and is the preferred method for retinopathy assessment.

External study · Thailand national programme

Prospective deployment of a deep-learning system at 9 primary care centres, 7,651 patients. Vision-threatening DR:

91.4%

95.4%
specificity
Retina-specialist over-readers
84.8%
sensitivity
95.5%

Different, externally developed system. Shown only as context for AI-assisted screening in Thailand. It is not evidence about this Workbench.

Sources: ICO Guidelines for Diabetic Eye Care (2017) §1, §2.1, §3.1.3. Ruamviboonsuk P, et al. Lancet Digit Health 2022;4(4):e235–e244, numbers checked against the published abstract.

Act I · PositioningCurrent product

What it is, and what it is not

It is

An assistive review workstation

  • Optional AI evidence shown beside the retinal image
  • One explicit clinician DR grade for every image
  • Lesion ROIs a clinician can confirm, correct or remove
  • An auditable record of who confirmed what, and when
  • A way to build task-specific DR-ready and Lesion-ready datasets
It is not

A diagnostic or decision-making device

  • Not autonomous diagnosis, and not a substitute for reading
  • Not a referral, follow-up or treatment decision-maker
  • Not patient-facing result reporting
  • Not a calibrated probability: scores are model scores
  • Not a regulated medical device
Rule

Every image is finished by a clinician’s explicit confirmation. Nothing is confirmed automatically.

Sources: README, AGENTS.md scientific boundaries, clinician manual §Before You Begin (baseline 957b71d). Framing adapted from the owner ophthalmologist deck and corrected to current behaviour.

Act II · Clinical contextClinical reference · ICO 2017

DR severity in five steps

0
No apparent DR
No abnormalities
1
Mild NPDR
Microaneurysms only
2
Moderate NPDR
Microaneurysms and other signs (dot and blot hemorrhages, hard exudates, cotton wool spots), but less than severe NPDR
3
Severe NPDR
Any of: intraretinal hemorrhages ≥20 in each quadrant · definite venous beading in 2 quadrants · IRMA in 1 quadrant; no signs of PDR
4
Proliferative DR
Severe NPDR and one or more of: neovascularization · vitreous or preretinal hemorrhage
Diabetic macular edema, assessed separately

No DME, non-central-involved or central-involved. It needs three-dimensional assessment (slit-lamp or stereo photography, OCT). The Workbench does not produce a DME output.

ICO 2017 guidance: re-examination / referral
Clinical context · not software behaviour
ClassificationHigh-resourceLow / intermediateReferral
Mild NPDR6–12 months1–2 yearsNot required
Moderate NPDR3–6 months6–12 monthsRequired
Severe NPDR< 3 months< 3 monthsRequired
PDR< 1 month< 1 monthRequired

Source: ICO Guidelines for Diabetic Eye Care (2017), Table 1, Table 2a/2b (“in cases where diabetes is controlled”). © ICO 2017; non-commercial local adaptation with credit. Workbench grades 0–4 follow this order; the RETFound head uses the APTOS 2019 0–4 scale.

Clinical signs, and what the model sees

MicroaneurysmsMA · Microaneurysm
Dot and blot hemorrhagesHE · Hemorrhage
Hard exudatesEX · Hard exudate
Cotton wool spotsSE · Soft exudate
Venous beadingNot modelled

Neovascularization (NVD / NVE)Not modelled
Vitreous or preretinal hemorrhageNot modelled
Real retinal photographNo overlay drawn. This presentation does not annotate findings for effect.

Signs that define severe NPDR and PDR are outside the current lesion model. The clinician grade must cover them.

Act II · Model 1 of 2Upstream modelWorkbench role

RETFound, the global grade

What it was developed on

1.6 million

unlabelled retinal images, learned by self-supervised pretraining (no diagnoses needed)

Colour fundus photographs904,170
90.2% Moorfields (MEH-MIDAS) · 9.8% Kaggle EyePACS
OCT scans736,442
85.2% Moorfields (MEH-MIDAS) · 14.8% public OCT dataset
What it contributes to the Workbench
  • Adapter: retfound-aptos5, the official RETFound five-class head fine-tuned on APTOS 2019, a public colour fundus DR grading set
  • Output: one global DR grade suggestion (0–4) and a model score for colour fundus input
  • In the UI: shown under DR assessment and as the AI suggestion line; never pre-selected
  • Boundary: the score is not a calibrated clinical probability. Research / non-commercial licence (CC BY-NC 4.0)

Upstream results were reported on public datasets. They are not local clinical validation of this Workbench.

Sources: Zhou Y, et al. Nature 2023;622:156–163 (pretraining data composition). rmaphoh/RETFound, pinned revision ae9a9ecf, BENCHMARK.md (APTOS 2019 checkpoint). Workbench: dr_support/providers/retfound.py, clinician manual.

Act II · Model 2 of 2Upstream modelWorkbench role

PRISM-DR, the lesion boxes

What it was developed on

IDRiD

Indian Diabetic Retinopathy Image Dataset, lesion-segmentation set: a small, expert-annotated colour fundus collection used for training and held-out testing.

MA
specialist
HE
specialist
EX
specialist
SE
specialist

Each lesion type has its own detector (five-fold ensemble); outputs are merged. The authors also report external checks on e-ophtha, DDR and TJDR without fine-tuning.

What it contributes to the Workbench
  • Adapter: prism-dr-5fold, pinned upstream release
  • Output: candidate lesion boxes in original-image pixels, each with class and model score
  • In the UI: dashed class-coloured boxes a clinician may confirm, correct or remove; untouched suggestions stay AI evidence
  • Boundary: an empty result does not prove absence. Scores are not probabilities

Upstream IDRiD metrics are not local product performance. Licences: code MIT; Ultralytics AGPL-3.0; weights released for academic use.

Sources: Özeren Z, Uyar T. PRISM-DR. arXiv:2607.19864 (2026), with dataset roles checked in the official zubeyrozeren/PRISM-DR README (pinned 79637440). Workbench: dr_support/providers/prism.py, contracts LABELS.

Act II · Human authorityCurrent product behaviour

Evidence and decisions, never merged

L1

Original admitted image

Source bytes are never changed. Identity is recorded by SHA-256.

L2

Analysis representation

Only if a derivative is needed for inference. Its provenance is kept separately and coordinates map back to original pixels.

L3

AI evidence

Model identity, revision, class, score and geometry, stored as returned. Human edits never overwrite it.

L4

Clinician decisions

Confirmed image context · final DR grade (kept, changed, or given without a model) · confirmed annotation set with reviewer, time and hash.

When a clinician corrects an ROI

The corrected box is shown as clinician corrected, without the model’s score. If PRISM-DR said “Hemorrhage · 0.55” and you change it to hard exudate, it never reads “Hard exudate · 0.55”.

The original AI class, score, box and model stay in the review record. A removed suggestion stays in the audit record.

Sources: AGENTS.md (immutability, provenance); clinician manual §Confirm DR Grade (grade provenance), §Annotation Editor (score meaning), §Confirm Annotation (annotation-set hash); dr_support/images.py analysis derivatives.

Act III · Operation manualCurrent workflow

One line, three confirmations

Confirmation milestone Optional
No escalation step

There is no normal “Escalate” or senior-review action. If you are not ready to decide, the grade simply stays Not confirmed.

Act III · Safety boundariesCurrent product behaviourClinical reference

Uncertain is never normal

Ungradable ≠ normal

Image quality is a clinician judgement; the Workbench has no automated “normal” verdict. ICO 2017 advises referral when retinal assessment is inadequate, unless there is obviously no DR or only mild NPDR.

Empty detection ≠ no lesion

No PRISM-DR boxes does not prove absence. Confirming an empty annotation set records that the set was reviewed, not that lesions are absent.

Model score ≠ probability

RETFound and PRISM-DR scores are uncalibrated model outputs. A corrected ROI never inherits the model’s score.

No model ≠ no workflow

If the Model API is unavailable, every step still works manually. Non-fundus DICOM is shown as Unsupported modality and never sent to the models.

Sources: AGENTS.md scientific boundaries; clinician manual §Review, §Confirm Annotation, §Troubleshooting; ICO 2017 §2.1 (inadequate retinal assessment). Screenshot: Playwright capture, baseline 957b71d.

Act III · Your inputDiscussion · proposed next steps

What we need from you

01 · Workflow fit

Is one line per image right?

Where does the flow slow you down? Is confirming image context before grading acceptable in your setting?

02 · Lesion taxonomy

Are MA, HE, EX and SE enough?

Should “soft exudate” read as cotton wool spot? How should unmodelled signs (venous beading, IRMA, new vessels) be recorded?

03 · Uncertainty display

How should doubt be shown?

Ungradable images, low-score boxes, and model unavailability: what wording and visual cues help you most?

04 · Validation priorities

What would convince you?

Reference standard, independent double reading of a pilot set, agreement measures, and which endpoints matter first.

Proposed

A shared grading and labelling guide, a pilot double-reading exercise, and a named clinical advisor. These are proposals for discussion, not completed work.

Source: owner ophthalmologist deck (requests to the clinical team), reframed as open questions. No outcome or validation result is claimed.
